answer: Anchor every identity to one distinct physical machine. Each epoch, an agent's secure enclave emits a hardware-attested pulse, signed by a factory-burned key that cannot be copied, proving the same device still hosts it. A farm of software clones cannot fake this signal: a thousand fake identities demand a thousand real machines, so the attack's marginal cost jumps from near-zero software to linear hardware. One device's attestation reused across identities is caught on-ledger. No ivory-tower software trick defeats it; each ghost pays full hardware price, exceeding per-identity reward.
